key_big: Divisible by 9 ⇔ the digit sum is divisible by 9
key_sub: By 4: last two digits; by 8: last three; by 11: alternating sum.
body_html:
How it works

Divisibility tests: by 3 or 9, use the digit sum; by 4, the last two digits; by 8, the last three digits; by 6, test 2 and 3; by 11, the alternating sum of digits.

A number and its digit sum leave the same remainder when divided by 9 (or 3).

A sum is odd when it has an odd number of odd terms; a product is odd only when every factor is odd.

Example

Is 7,128 divisible by 8?

Last three digits: 128 = 8 × 16

Answer: Yes

Example

Find the remainder when 52,417 is divided by 9.

Digit sum = 19

19 = 2 × 9 + 1

Answer: 1

Common mistakes

  • Testing divisibility by 4 with the last digit only.
  • Using the plain digit sum for 11 instead of the alternating sum.
  • Thinking an even number of numbers always has an even sum.

faq.q: How do you check divisibility by 11?
faq.a: Add the digits in odd places and in even places; if the difference is 0 or a multiple of 11, the number is divisible by 11.

faq.q: Why does the digit sum give the remainder for 9?
faq.a: Because 10, 100, 1,000 … each leave remainder 1 when divided by 9.

faq.q: When is a sum of whole numbers odd?
faq.a: When it contains an odd number of odd numbers.
